rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Self-report + self-audit charity
rules_evaluated.evidence: L29-32: "Check the copy landed" verifies only against Claude's stated confirmation ("The output should name both CLAUDE.local.md and observations/"), never against the artefact itself (e.g. `ls` the worktree path). Harm the rule guards: a silently failed or partial `cp` gets reported as done and goes uncaught, and the very next exercise opens inside this worktree assuming the rules are really there.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add a one-line artefact-level check (e.g. `ls ../<repo-name>-m5/CLAUDE.local.md`) alongside reading Claude's summary — low-cost given the mechanical scope, author to weigh against the file's explicit 15-min/no-judgement-call budget.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Per-exercise leap test - 3 observable Monday outcomes
rules_evaluated.evidence: Maintainer block (L40-51) has no leap-test list at all. Harm the rule guards: without a falsifiable Monday-outcome statement, a trainer/auditor can't tell what this exercise is supposed to leave the student able to do on their own repo versus merely having watched happen once.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Add 3 observable outcomes (e.g. "forks a sibling worktree from a named starting commit", "copies gitignored personal rules/observations across by hand when Claude's default pass misses one", "recovers the fork point from merge-base when the run-coordinates block is gone") to the maintainer block.

Flag as a maintainer question rather than a body fix: is body-placement an acceptable satisfaction of §47's letter, or does the maintainer-block naming need to happen even when duplicative?
